answer: Prism-Seeded Enrollment Windows. Each enrollment round derives a seed from a public verifiable random function beacon after the round closes, then hashes seed with candidate keys to assign each identity a quill slot in a fixed-size window. Only slot holders may submit, so an attacker cannot precompute placements before the seed is revealed. A failed voyage across rounds costs one distinct hardware attestation plus a fresh video challenge, making mass pre-registration pay per attempt with no guaranteed payoff.
